correctness.rationale: The Gaussian first-column ratio T=c/a is standard Cauchy. Partial row pivoting maps it to R=T if |T|≤1, otherwise 1/T, giving density 2/(π(1+r²)) on (-1,1). The independent second-column Gaussians produce Z|R=r~N(0,1+r²); direct integration yields CF, all integer moments, variance and fourth moment; a Cauchy-square ratio makes unpivoted variance infinite. Numerical independent check sampled 200,000 matrices and separately computed exact second/fourth normalizers, agreeing within Monte Carlo variation.
risks: Continuous Gaussian assumption and exact arithmetic; no claims about floating point error or high-dimensional GEPP.
Monte Carlo is corroboration, not proof of distribution.

final_claim: For iid N(0,1) real 2×2 matrices, GEPP final Schur pivot Z has truncated-Cauchy-normal mixture law, even moments 4(2m−1)!!/π ∑_{j=0}^{m−1} C(m−1,j)/(2j+1), variance4/π, standardized kurtosisπ; unpivoted final pivot has infinite variance.
limitations: Only n=2, Gaussian real entries, exact arithmetic, and the last scalar pivot; no statements about upper-triangular entry growth in n>2.
